# Route accounting {#sec-method}

**Setting.** A model processes a prompt and generates text. An intervention changes the
information at a set of **source** positions \(S\), and its effect is measured at a
later **target** position \(t\) where that information is used. The positions strictly
between them, \(M\), include the end of the prompt and the tokens generated so far.
Every intervention is an **all-layer state edit**: the residual stream at every layer of
each source position is replaced by the states of a *donor* prompt that differs only in
the content under study (a first line with a different rhyme, a list in a different
order), while the prompt text is unchanged. The outcome is a log-odds contrast at the
target,

$$
R \;=\; \log \sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{\rm donor}} p(v\mid\cdot) \;-\; \log \sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{\rm orig}} p(v\mid\cdot),
$$

where \(\mathcal V_{\rm donor}\) and \(\mathcal V_{\rm orig}\) are the tokens
consistent with the donor's and the original content, for example the single-token
perfect rhymes of each rhyme word. Effects are changes in \(R\) relative to the unedited
run; positive values move the target toward the donor.

**Emission and persistence.** The edit can change what the model writes, and the
written tokens are read back. Let \(g_0\) and \(g_1\) be the texts generated with the
edit off and on, and \(R(i,g)\) the outcome with the edit in state \(i\in\{0,1\}\) and
the text fixed to \(g\). Then

$$
\underbrace{R(1,g_1)-R(0,g_0)}_{\text{total}}
\;=\;
\underbrace{R(0,g_1)-R(0,g_0)}_{\text{emission}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{R(1,g_1)-R(0,g_1)}_{\text{persistence}} .
$$

**Emission** replays the edited words with the edit off. **Persistence** is what the
edit does with the text held fixed. We also report persistence with the original text,
\(R(1,g_0)-R(0,g_0)\), the other order of the decomposition, where the two differ. For a
binary mediator such as the article *a/an*, emission factorizes into the change in the
mediator policy times the leverage of the mediator (@sec-emission; Appendix
@sec-app-sixcell).

**Paths within persistence.** The target can read the edited source itself (**direct
retrieval**), or intermediate positions can read it and pass it on (an **indirect
path**). We separate the two by clamping states. Let \(h^{0}\) and \(h^{1}\) be the
per-layer states of the clean and the edited run, both with the text fixed, and write
\(R[\,S\!\leftarrow\!a,\;G\!\leftarrow\!b\,]\) for the outcome when the source receives
the states of run \(a\) and a group \(G\subseteq M\) those of run \(b\), at every layer,
with all other positions recomputed. With \(R_0\) the clean outcome,

$$
\begin{aligned}
P &= R[S\!\leftarrow\!1] - R_0 &&\text{persistence,}\\
D &= R[S\!\leftarrow\!1,\;M\!\leftarrow\!0] - R_0 &&\text{direct retrieval (every intermediate position clean),}\\
T &= R[M\!\leftarrow\!1] - R_0 &&\text{indirect paths (source clean, intermediates as in the edited run),}\\
\Delta &= P - D - T &&\text{interaction (additivity gap).}
\end{aligned}
$$

Because the intermediate states are overwritten at every layer, \(D\) reaches the target
only through its own attention to the source, and \(T\) only through intermediate
positions. For a group \(G\) we report its **interventional sufficiency**,
\(\mathrm{Suf}(G)=R[G\!\leftarrow\!1]-R_0\), the effect of the group alone, and its
**interventional necessity**,
\(\mathrm{Nec}(G)=P-\big(R[S\!\leftarrow\!1,\,G\!\leftarrow\!0]-R_0\big)\), the loss of
persistence when the group alone is reset to its clean states. When paths combine
additively, the two agree and shares partition the effect. Where the interaction is
large (at most 33% of persistence, in Gemma 3 27B couplets), shares are not exclusive,
and we report both measures and their average, the Shapley value [@shapley1953]. Shares
are divided by the persistence of the same run unless another denominator is named, and
intervals are item-bootstrap 95% intervals [@efron1994bootstrap].

**Path names.** We split \(M\) into three groups by position, not by any hypothesis
about their content, and name the indirect path through each. The **stored copy** passes
through the prompt positions right after the source line (in couplets, the token that
ends line 1 and the chat template). The **late lookup** passes through the three
positions just before the target; it is the late retrieval of @hanna2026latent read in
two steps. **Relay** passes through the remaining positions of the generated text; it is
the path monitoring is concerned with. Information is **looked up** when it arrives by
direct retrieval, the stored copy or the late lookup. Where a group was not split
further, we name it and call its effect the indirect path through it. These names and
their colours (@fig-overview) are fixed throughout.

## Positive control: induction {#sec-control}

A decomposition that never reports an indirect path could be blind to one. In a
repeated sequence \(\ldots A\,B\ldots A\), a previous-token head writes "preceded by
\(A\)" into the position of \(B\), and an induction head at the second \(A\) finds that
position and copies \(B\) [@olsson2022induction]. Information about the first \(A\)
therefore reaches the prediction through an intermediate position. We edit the first
\(A\) in 100 random sequences and measure \(\log p(B)\) at the second \(A\). The
criterion, committed before the first result, was an indirect path above 80% of
persistence with direct retrieval near zero. It holds cleanly in Qwen3 1.7B to 14B:
direct retrieval is 1 to 3% and the indirect path 108 to 137%, the excess over 100%
being an interaction. In Gemma 3 12B and 27B direct retrieval is 0.4%, but conflicting
edited positions lower the all-position cell to 53 to 55% (the key position alone gives
145 to 156%). Qwen3-32B and the Qwen3.5 hybrids also read the source directly (10 to
31%). In every model the indirect path is the largest path (Appendix @sec-app-control). The key position lies right after the source, so this path resembles
a stored copy more than relay. What the control establishes is that route accounting
detects an effect that arrives through an intermediate position. Relay is the same kind
of path through different positions: with the generated text fixed, generated tokens
are ordinary context positions, and the clamp is the same operation at any position.
The retrieval-dominated results that follow are therefore informative negatives, not a
blind spot of the method.

**Models and protocol.** We study Qwen3 1.7B to 32B, dense with full attention
[@yang2025qwen3]; Gemma 3 1B to 27B, which interleaves five sliding-window layers with a
1,024-token window per global layer [@gemma3]; Qwen3.5 4B, 9B and 27B, hybrids in which
three of every four layers are Gated DeltaNet recurrent layers [@qwen2026qwen35;
@yang2025gateddeltanet]; and Gemma 4 31B [@gemma4] for the hidden choice. We use
instruction-tuned checkpoints, with base checkpoints as checks, and disable thinking, so
the generated spans are short. After the initial couplet split, the design and decision
rule of every experiment were committed to the repository before its first result;
later additions are labelled post hoc (Appendix @sec-app-prereg). Materials and per-run
tables are in Appendix @sec-app-materials.
